questions.q: What's the difference between df["customer_name"] and df[["customer_name"]]?
options: The first returns a Series, the second returns a one-column DataFrame
They always return identical results
The first only works on numeric columns
The second deletes the column from df
questions.explain: A single column name returns a Series; a list of column names (even one item) returns a DataFrame.

questions.q: In orders.csv, how many rows does df[df["quantity"] < 0] return?
options: 1 — order 1014
0 — there are no negative quantities
20 — every row
2 — orders 1014 and 1005
questions.explain: Order 1014 (Marcus Ibeh, Insulated Bottle 1L) is the only row with a negative quantity, -1.

questions.q: When combining two conditions with & in a pandas boolean filter, why does each condition need its own parentheses?
options: Python's operator precedence doesn't evaluate bare == next to & the way you'd expect without them
Parentheses are purely stylistic and never actually required
& only works with exactly one condition
pandas requires parentheses only for string columns
questions.explain: Writing df[cond1 & cond2] without parens around each condition is a common source of errors.

questions.q: After df_indexed = df.set_index("order_id"), what does df_indexed.loc[1005] return?
options: The row labeled 1005 — the order with the missing customer_name, shown as NaN
The 1005th row by position, regardless of order_id
An error, because .loc only works with the default integer index
A count of how many rows have order_id greater than 1005
questions.explain: .loc looks up by label, and after set_index("order_id") the labels are order IDs; order 1005's customer_name shows as NaN.

questions.q: What does NaN represent in a pandas DataFrame?
options: A missing value
A negative number
A text string that failed to parse
The maximum value in a column
questions.explain: The blank customer_name field in the raw CSV for order 1005 became NaN once pandas loaded it.
